title: LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections
summary: Bookmark and refresh this page for the latest news, photos, videos, and analyses as Rappler closely follows the historic elections

blocks.text: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao is holding its first parliamentary elections on September 14, 2026, after being postponed at least four times: first in May 2022, then in May 2025, October 2025, and again in March 2026.

The historic polls are seen as a pivotal moment in the decades-long peace process in a region that was mired in conflict and socioeconomic and political challenges. The upcoming elections are also a test for the Bangsamoro transition and the institutions and systems established in the last seven years.
Bookmark and refresh this page for the latest news, photos, videos, and analyses as Rappler closely follows the regional elections.

17 hours ago
FACT CHECK: Ballots are not pre-shaded, secured for 2026 polls — Comelec

Several false posts claimed that municipal employees and teachers are pre-shading ballots ahead of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary elections on September 14. These posts are false.

The Commission on Elections debunked the false claim through a September 11 Facebook post, assuring that the election ballots are currently secured and vacuum-sealed inside the region’s municipal and city treasurers’ offices.
The commission said no pre-shading can happen, since ballots will only be opened on the day of the election.

blocks.text: Sep 9, 2026 5:59 PM PHT
FACT CHECK: No Turkish police deployed to secure BARMM polls
A September 6 Facebook post claims that Turkish police officers will be deployed to secure the upcoming BARMM parliamentary elections on September 14. This claim is false.

Election watchdog groups Independent Election Monitoring Center-BARMM and the Institute for Autonomy and Governance have debunked the claim, saying no foreign police force — including Turkey’s — can police another country’s elections.

blocks.text: Sep 8, 2026 7:55 PM PHT
NAMFREL releases pre-election assessment
Poll watchdog National Citizens’ Movement for Free Elections released on Tuesday, September 8, its pre-election assessment six days before the September 14 polls.
Below are some of its key findings:

items: [The Commission on Elections’] technical and logistical readiness is strong. The automated election system, ballot materials, and legal calendar are all assessed ready.

The principal risks to the election’s legitimacy are political, not mechanical. These include unresolved allegations of national-patronage interference in the [Moro Islamic Liberation Front] succession contest, and a widening gap between official and independently monitored security data.

Critical infrastructure deserves close attention in the final days. The Mindanao Grid enters E-Day week with thin power-reserve margins, and internet connectivity remains uneven across [Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao’s] provinces.

blocks.text: Sep 8, 2026 6:51 PM PHT
Prevent outside influence in Bangsamoro polls, groups urge Marcos

Civil society groups urged President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday, September 8, to prevent external actors from attempting to influence the outcome of the Bangsamoro parliamentary polls and undermine the autonomy the region fought hard for.

Duyog Bangsamoro, a coalition comprised of regional and national civic organizations, urged the national government to continue supporting the peace process “regardless of which parties win the elections.”
